subject: Post-call summary: token economics & cache impact synthesis for Retaily
messages:
From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@retaily.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — token volumes & next steps

Thanks for the demo earlier — good session. Two quick clarifications from our side so we can align on pricing: 

- Volume profile: our initial production cohort is ~1.8M active users monthly, but only ~0.6M will hit the ML surfaces we discussed. Estimated token mix: ~70% short queries (~50–150 tokens) and ~30% long form (~400–1200 tokens). Ballpark monthly generated tokens: 350M–600M depending on adoption curve.

- Budget: procurement has penciled a $6k–$20k/month target for model consumption (we know it’s wide). Target effective pricing target is under $10/1M tokens to meet our unit economics.

Specific ask: can you provide a concise effective unit-cost sensitivity showing our baseline per-1M price + the impact of a modest prefix/hot-prompt cache (we expect repeated prompts for category search) and the assumptions behind the hit-rate numbers? Attached earlier is our anonymized usage dump for March — looks like a lot of repeat prefixes.

Thanks,
Alex

---

alex.moore@retaily.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@retaily.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — token volumes & next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage dump. Quick synthesis from our side (high level):

1) Baseline unit price: for the curated model we demoed, the hosted list price is $12/1M tokens (this is the normal generation charge; embeddings and system tokens billed separately).

2) Cache strategy we recommend: two-tier approach — (a) prefix cache for deterministic, repeated prefixes (user intents like "find size X in red") and (b) a small hot-prompt cache for high-frequency completions. Both live in-memory at the edge; prefix cache avoids runtime generation entirely for cached prompts.

3) Hit-rate assumptions (our conservative / expected / optimistic buckets based on similar retail customers):
   - Conservative: 12% prefix hit + 3% hot-prompt = 15% total
   - Expected: 22% prefix + 6% hot-prompt = 28% total
   - Optimistic: 35% prefix + 8% hot-prompt = 43% total

4) Effective $/1M calculation: simple model = (base_price * (1 - hit_rate)) + cache_overhead. For your baseline we estimate a small cache-serving overhead (~$0.50/1M tokens) to account for memory/edge bandwidth and small proxy costs.

   Examples (base $12/1M):
   - Conservative (15%): 12*(1 - 0.15) + 0.5 = $10.7/1M
   - Expected (28%): 12*(1 - 0.28) + 0.5 = $9.16/1M
   - Optimistic (43%): 12*(1 - 0.43) + 0.5 = $7.34/1M

5) Budget mapping: for your target range ($6k–$20k/month):
   - At 350M tokens/month, expected-case cost = 350 * 9.16/1000 = ~$3,206/mo (well within range) — note this scales linearly with tokens.
   - At 600M tokens/month, expected-case = 600 * 9.16/1000 = ~$5,496/mo.

These numbers are illustrative — they show you hit your <$10/1M target with our expected cache behavior and a modest overhead.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: can you run the attached usage.csv through the quick hit-rate estimator and share the workbook (estimate by prefix frequency buckets)?
- Grace: can we prepare a short pilot proposal (2–4 week, canary to 5k users) with instrumentation (prefix reuse, median latency, cache eviction) and a fixed pilot price?
- Alex: if procurement wants an SOW-style cost table for review, we can format the three hit-rate scenarios into a procurement-ready sheet.

I'll attach the quick savings model so you can tweak hit rates; Karthik will own the numbers.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood_cache_savings_model.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — token volumes & next steps

Alex / Sean — ran a first pass on the CSV. Quick findings (very rough, will refine):

- Top 2k unique prefixes account for ~27% of total calls in the sample window. If those map well to prefix keys (we may need normalization/templating), that supports a 25–30% prefix hit rate in steady state.
- Hot-prompt candidates (top 500 completions) add another ~5–7% opportunity if we cache deterministic small completions.
- Long-form generation (the 30% of tokens) has low repeatability; caching helps more on short/query flows.

I've uploaded the workbook with a bucketed estimator and a column showing conservative/expected/optimistic hit-rate assumptions per prefix frequency band. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_redwood_retaily_notes

Proposed pilot: 3 weeks, 5k MAU scoped to product searches and cart assistant. We'll instrument exact prefix reuse and return a measured hit-rate; if measured hit-rate >= 22% we convert to a standard pricing commitment (TBD).

Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
